findings.title: Reentrancy in NativeSwitchboardBase.registerSiblingSlug(uint32,uint256,uint256,uint256,address)
findings.description:
The function calls out to another contract before it finishes updating its own state. A malicious callee can re-enter while the state is half-written; no ether moves in the reentrant path itself, but the stale state can be abused. findings.title: ERC20.permit(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint8,bytes32,bytes32) uses timestamp for comparisons
findings.description:
Logic depends on block.timestamp, which miners can nudge by a few seconds (informational). Slither: ERC20.permit(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint8,bytes32,bytes32) (lib/solmate/src/tokens/ERC20.sol#116-160) uses timestamp for comparisons
	Dangerous comparisons:
